{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement (we represent the Customer)

---

## Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. Nineteen rules were assessed: eight areas are compliant and require no redline, nine are deviations requiring negotiation, and one (Vendor indemnification) is missing entirely.

The agreement is strong in several respects that we should preserve: Customer ownership of Customer Data and Deliverables (§ 14), our unrestricted assignment and change-of-control rights (§ 24), audit protections (§ 22), New York law and venue with no arbitration (§ 28), renewal mechanics with a capped uplift (§ 8.2–8.3), and Vendor insurance including USD 5,000,000 cyber cover (§ 18).

The risk is concentrated in four places. First, § 20 is a one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity with **no Vendor indemnity at all**, including no IP infringement indemnity; § 9.3 already cross-refers to a "Section 20.5" that does not exist. Second, § 21.1 caps each party's liability at Fees paid in a single month "without exception," which both falls far below our floor and overrides the Excluded Claims regime in § 21.3. Third, § 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights," which renders our § 9.4 convenience right illusory and triggers three separate rules (minimum commitment, liquidated damages, termination for convenience). Fourth, §§ 2.2 and 12.4 impose exclusivity and a 24-month, all-territory non-compete on us — both of which contradict § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no such commitments.

We also note internal inconsistency throughout: § 13.1 conflicts with §§ 13.2, 13.3 and 24.1; § 11.1 conflicts with §§ 11.2, 11.3 and 10.1; and there is no order-of-precedence clause to resolve these conflicts. Several of the deviations should therefore be framed to counsel as conforming edits that align the operative clauses with provisions Vendor has already accepted.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | § 20 (20.1) | One-way, unlimited Customer indemnity for "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services"; no Vendor indemnity, including no IP infringement indemnity (walk-away). § 9.3 cross-refers to a non-existent § 20.5. Add Vendor defence/indemnity (third-party IP, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused compromise of Customer Data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice/control/cooperation procedure, customary exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in a new § 20.5; narrow Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law. Indemnities are already Excluded Claims under § 21.3, so no super-cap change is needed. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 21.1 | Cap is Fees "actually paid" in the one month preceding the event, "without exception" — below our floor (greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000) and below the six-month walk-away threshold. "Fees" (§ 1.5) excludes taxes, expenses, credits and one-time implementation charges, so a one-month measure is close to illusory against a Security Incident. "Without exception" also pulls indemnities, confidentiality, data protection, security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside the cap, overriding § 21.3. Reset to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and reinstate Excluded Claims as uncapped. §§ 21.2–21.4 are compliant and unchanged. |
| 3 | Critical | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 (and 14.2–14.4, 13.2, 1.4, 1.8, 15.1) | Customer owns Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and independently developed IP, with only a limited processing right to Vendor; Deliverables assigned to Customer; embedded Vendor Technology covered by the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence in § 13.2; joint ownership barred absent signed instrument; § 15.1 bars sale, advertising use, data combination and model training without consent. No redline. |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | **Deviation** | § 2.2 | Vendor as our "sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services" for the entire term, with no category limit, time limit or performance exit — walk-away position. Directly conflicts with § 12.3. Delete § 2.2 and let § 12.3 govern; fallback of a 12-month, category-limited commitment with an SLA-failure exit offered in comment. |
| 5 | High | NONCOMPETE | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | 24-month post-term, all-territory, undefined-scope non-compete binding Customer — beyond the walk-away threshold; contradicts § 12.3. Delete; narrowed fallback (single named product, term only, 12 months, carve-outs) offered in comment. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.1 | USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights" operates as a Customer-payable penalty; conflicts with § 9.4 and the cap-free payment carve-out in § 21.3. Delete so we pay only for Services ordered and received; fallback of an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees offered in comment. § 27.3 confirms termination "without penalty." |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 2.1 (§ 9.4 compliant) | § 9.4 alone meets our position (30 days' notice, refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience right). But § 2.1's "without reduction or termination rights" language, absent any order-of-precedence clause, can be read to override § 9.4 — or leave us liable for the full unpaid minimum on exit, an effective cost of up to three years' committed spend (walk-away). Carve terminations out of § 2.1 so the commitment reduces pro rata with no shortfall or early-termination amount; § 9.4 needs no edit. |
| 8 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 13.1 | Licence to Customer alone, excluding Affiliates and contractors, non-transferable and revocable at Vendor's sole discretion — walk-away position; conflicts with §§ 13.2, 13.3 and 24.1. Extend to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, remove discretionary revocation by tying suspension/revocation to § 13.3, and confirm transferability. |
| 9 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (and 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Customer may assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor on notice only; Vendor restricted asymmetrically and barred from assigning to our direct competitor; § 24.3 consent limited to "other assignments"; § 24.4 confirms our change of control gives Vendor no termination, suspension, repricing, acceleration or service-reduction right. No redline. |
| 10 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitment | **Deviation** | § 2.1 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay with express denial of reduction or termination rights — walk-away position; conflicts with §§ 9.4 and 12.3. Replace with payment for Services ordered or used, consistent with §§ 7.1 and 9.4; fallback of a 12-month reducible commitment with true-up offered in comment. |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | **Deviation** | § 11.1 | Requires immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support — walk-away position; contradicts §§ 11.2, 11.3 and the "agreed transition period" in § 10.1. Replace with up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, subordinated to the 11.2/11.3 return-then-delete sequence; 90 days available as fallback. |
| 12 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 19.2 | Deliverable conformance warranty limited to fifteen days, after which Vendor has no correction or refund obligation — cuts off the § 19.4 remedy and guts § 19.1. Short of the preferred 12 months (software) / 90 days (services) and the 90/30 fallback. Extend to 12 months / 90 days and delete the sunset, preserving the non-exclusive § 19.4 remedy. §§ 19.1, 19.3–19.5 otherwise compliant. |
| 13 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (and 22.2–22.3) | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%; no direct access to our systems, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material or another supplier's confidential information; findings are Customer Confidential Information. § 23 has a heading only, with no operative text. No redline. |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (and 28.2–28.3) | New York law, CISG disapplied; exclusive jurisdiction in New York County state and federal courts. No arbitration anywhere in the document. Mutual escalation step does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings, and injunctive relief to protect confidential information or IP is preserved. No redline. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No MFN language beyond § 12.3, which confirms we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment; § 7.1 (fixed Fees) and § 8.3 (capped uplift) impose no matching obligation on us and in fact constrain Vendor pricing. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No non-solicit, no-hire or non-inducement covenant binds Customer; § 12.3 expressly preserves our right to hire anyone responding to general recruitment. No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (and 8.1, 8.3) | Twelve-month renewals, 30 days' opt-out notice, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension if missed; uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice, excluding prepaid periods; fixed three-year initial term. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (and 18.2) | CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber and privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability USD 1M; term plus one year. § 18.2 adds reputable insurers, certificates on request, notice of cancellation or material reduction, and confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities (so § 21 caps are not undercut). No redline. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following findings sit at the playbook's walk-away positions. Each should be resolved before signature; we should not proceed on the current drafting.

1. **No Vendor indemnity, including no IP infringement indemnity (§ 20).** The absence of an IP infringement indemnity is the playbook walk-away position, compounded by an unlimited one-way Customer indemnity and a broken cross-reference in § 9.3 to a non-existent § 20.5.
2. **One-month liability cap applied "without exception" (§ 21.1).** Below even the six-month walk-away threshold, and the "without exception" language collapses the Excluded Claims regime in § 21.3 — leaving data, security, confidentiality, IP, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud claims capped at a near-illusory amount.
3. **Illusory termination for convenience (§ 2.1 read against § 9.4).** With no order-of-precedence clause, the effective exit cost is up to three years of committed spend against a fallback ceiling of three months' fees — no real convenience right in a multi-year term.
4. **Three-year take-or-pay minimum with no reduction or termination rights (§ 2.1).** Walk-away under the minimum-commitment rule, and independently objectionable as a Customer-payable penalty.
5. **Term-long exclusivity as sole analytics provider (§ 2.2).** No category limit, no time limit, no performance-based exit.
6. **24-month post-term, all-territory non-compete on Customer (§ 12.4).** Beyond the 12-month post-term / defined-scope walk-away threshold.
7. **Licence to Customer alone, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion (§ 13.1).** Excludes Affiliates and contractors and is non-transferable — walk-away position.
8. **Immediate cessation of assistance and deletion of Customer Data on termination (§ 11.1).** No export or migration support — walk-away position.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline and playbook comments** covering the nine deviations and the missing Vendor indemnity, in the priority order above. Each edit is drafted as the minimal change that reaches our preferred position, with the fallback stated in the comment where one exists (exclusivity, non-compete, LD/early-termination fee, minimum commitment, transition period, warranty duration).
2. **Lead with the § 20 indemnity package and the § 21.1 cap.** These are the two items with no acceptable fallback. We should also flag to Vendor that § 9.3 is currently unworkable without the new § 20.5, which gives us a drafting-integrity argument alongside the commercial one.
3. **Address § 2.1 once, on all three grounds.** The take-or-pay clause drives the MINCOMMIT, LD and T4C findings. Our primary ask is deletion; if Vendor needs a commercial minimum, the negotiated landing should at minimum carve terminations out so § 9.4 operates and the commitment reduces pro rata.
4. **Use § 12.3 as leverage on §§ 2.2 and 12.4.** Vendor has already acknowledged in § 12.3 that we made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. Deleting §§ 2.2 and 12.4 (and § 2.1's minimum) is a conforming edit, not a new concession.
5. **Raise the internal-conflict point and request an order-of-precedence clause.** §§ 13.1 v. 13.2/13.3/24.1, § 11.1 v. 11.2/11.3/10.1, § 2.1 v. 9.4, and §§ 2.2/12.4 v. 12.3 all conflict. Even where we win the redline, a precedence clause reduces residual interpretive risk. We should also ask Vendor to confirm whether § 23 (Records and Customer Assurance), which currently contains a heading with no operative text, is intended to be blank.
6. **Confirm commercial sign-off on the fallbacks** — particularly any residual minimum commitment, any early-termination fee, and the transition-assistance period and rate basis — before we concede from the preferred positions.
7. **Preserve the compliant provisions.** §§ 14, 24, 22, 28, 8.2–8.3, 18, 12.3 and 19.1/19.3–19.5 meet or exceed our playbook; we should resist any Vendor attempt to reopen them as trade bait.

*Note on scope: this memo reflects only the findings supplied and the sections cited in them. No provision outside those findings has been assessed.*"}
